\begin{example}[A non-distributive Polar Semiring]\label{ex:nondistributive}
Let $X=\{\ev,a,b,c,\ew\}$ be the five-element modular lattice $M_3$, with $\ev$ the least element, $\ew$ the greatest, and $a,b,c$ pairwise incomparable. Define the polarity by
\[
  \dstar{\ev}=\ew,\qquad \dstar{\ew}=\ev,\qquad \dstar{a}=a,\qquad \dstar{b}=b,\qquad \dstar{c}=c,
\]
and let $\eo:=a$, with the tensor given by the following table (the join is the lattice join):
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
\otimes & \ev & a & b & c & \ew \\ \hline
\ev & \ev & \ev & \ev & \ev & \ev \\
a & \ev & a & b & c & \ew \\
b & \ev & b & a & c & \ew \\
c & \ev & c & c & \ev & c \\
\ew & \ev & \ew & \ew & c & \ew \\
\end{array}
\]
All eleven axioms of \Cref{def:ps} hold, yet
\[
  a\vee(b\wedge c)=a\vee\ev=a\quad\text{whereas}\quad(a\vee b)\wedge(a\vee c)=\ew\wedge\ew=\ew .
\]
Hence the induced lattice of a Polar Semiring need not be distributive.
\end{example}
